Dear Simon,

I took the exam in the end of May, and the part 2 was about 'describe a time when you received a service that you were not satisfied with.'

Thank you for your great website. I have learnt so much from your website, but I think that would be a good idea if you kindly give some focus on this topic too, so that we can also get prepared for this one.

comments.author: Simon
comments.text:
FROM SIMON (continued):

Here are my suggested versions:

1) In the age of the Internet, the options are endless.

2) If this website didn't exist, my studies would definitely be affected.

3) If YouTube ceased to exist, I would struggle to find the information that I need.

4) I don't think I would be able to keep my skills up to date if YouTube didn't exist.

5) Also, my life wouldn't be so easy if I had to depend on CDs.

comments.author: Simon
comments.text:
FROM SIMON:

First I'll explain the main problem(s) with each sentence.

1) This sentence is here because of the word 'plethora', which sounds too pompous and forced in this context. I wanted to see if people had read the lesson below (which contains a comment from an IELTS examiner):

https://ielts-simon.com/ielts-help-and-english-pr/2019/05/ielts-advice-big-words-dont-impress.html

2 - 5) These four sentences contain mistakes involving conditionals. Check the verbs carefully!

comments.author: Hung Nguyen
comments.text:
1. In the age of the internet, there are a lot of options.

2. If this website didn't exist, then my study would be affected.

3. If YouTube ceased to exist, I would find myself struggling to find the much-needed information.

4. I think it would be impossible for me to be more up-to-date and skillful if there was nothing like Youtube.

5. Life isn't also much easier and more flexible now than before if we depend much on CDs.

comments.author: HYS
comments.text:
1. Improved: Don't use words like "plethora" in speaking part 1&2, or even part 3. They sound forced and pretentious. Examiners know you try to impress them, but using those big words may actually have a bad impact on your score.

In the age of the internet, there are plenty of/ loads of options.

2. Corrected: Second conditional

If this website didn't* exist, then definitely my study would be affected.

3. Corrected: Second conditional

If YouTube ceased* to exist, I would* find myself struggling to find much-needed information.

4. Improved & Corrected: Second conditional & "nothing like"

I think it would* be impossible* to keep myself updated with the lastest news and trends in my field if there was* no* Youtube

if YouTube didn't exist.

5. Improved & Corrected: Second conditional

Life also wouldn't* be so easy* and flexible like now. It would be like when we used to depend mainly on offline resources such as CDs, physical books and magazines, what have you.

comments.author: lara
comments.text:
Re (1)

"a plethora of" is marked as formal. https://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/a-plethora-of-something

"plenty of" is common spoken vocabulary and means the same thing: https://www.ldoceonline.com/dictionary/plenty
